gaps: Weight shift and leg/hip/shoulder relationships now have multiple directly readable educational texts. Foot pressure, joint loading and balance mechanics still lack accessible, specialized portrait instruction; more searches found mostly self-published generic articles without sufficiently verified teaching credentials.

Need accessible demonstrations that compare pose variants with the same subject, camera framing and lighting, then explain the visible tradeoffs. No referenced demonstration video has been watched in this scan.

Hands and prop interaction now have cosplay-specific coverage for bare expressive hands and a sword grip. A cosplay specialist explicitly says to discuss movement limitations and plan around costume, but no accessible source here explains glove, sleeve, skirt or armor biomechanics; do not formalize mechanics without further evidence. Nikon's lesson 11 is one instructor/source family, not broad consensus.
Gaze and facial expression evidence is currently weighted toward commercial headshots. Need contrasting editorial, narrative, character, candid and action portrait instruction before generalizing.
Need sources from professional portrait photographers in Chinese-language curricula; search results in this pass did not yield a sufficiently attributable primary teaching source to include.

No claims about body-type-specific posing, gender presentation, or universally flattering positions should be formalized from this scan; individual comfort, mobility, wardrobe and intended character expression require direct evidence and contextual evaluation.
